g.text: Where did each candy-jar estimate move?
Each arrow follows the average estimate of one observed group, using exactly the same respondents before and after revision.
The vertical line marks the true count. Movement toward zero improves the full-group estimate; tighter agreement alone is insufficient.

a.text: Source: Becker, Brackbill & Centola (2017) | doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1615978114 | Reanalysis: 28 Sep 2026

g.text: Each row is a different jar; these are 18 separate group-by-jar observations, not a single group changing conditions.
No outlier trimming. One private-control initial mean is elevated by extreme responses; the revision control is therefore essential.
The study used on-screen numerical feedback. It did not test shouting, and the candy brand is not identified here.
